import pytest
from src.access_policy import can_edit

def test_can_edit_admin_can_edit():
    assert can_edit('admin', True, False) is True
    assert can_edit('admin', False, False) is True
    assert can_edit('admin', True, True) is False

def test_can_edit_editor_can_edit_own():
    assert can_edit('editor', True, False) is True
    assert can_edit('editor', False, False) is False
    assert can_edit('editor', True, True) is False

def test_can_edit_editor_cannot_edit_others():
    assert can_edit('editor', False, False) is False

def test_can_edit_other_roles_cannot_edit():
    assert can_edit('viewer', True, False) is False
    assert can_edit('viewer', False, False) is False

def test_can_edit_locked_record():
    assert can_edit('admin', True, True) is False
    assert can_edit('editor', True, True) is False
    assert can_edit('editor', False, True) is False
    assert can_edit('viewer', True, True) is False
    assert can_edit('viewer', False, True) is False

def test_can_edit_invalid_input():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        can_edit(123, True, False)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        can_edit('admin', 'yes', False)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        can_edit('admin', True, 'no')

assumptions: The function can_edit is the only public API for access policy.
The input types are strictly enforced as per the contract.
targeted_requirements: Admins can edit any record regardless of ownership.
Editors can only edit records they own.
Locked records cannot be edited by anyone.
All other roles are denied editing access.
